lesson.menu_desc: Reading about a shop owner's money plan and talking about prices and numbers -- how much / how many
lesson.subtitle: Lesson 8 -- Money Talk
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Camillo Furlan Alfredini | Lesson 8 -- Money Talk
lesson.grammar_point: how much / how many (countable and uncountable) + big numbers

listenings.text: This week at Max Motors: big prices, small payments! How much is the new family car? Only twenty-eight thousand dollars. How many colors are there? Six. And this week, the first service at our shop is free. Come and see our three hundred cars. Max Motors, open every day from nine to seven.

Hi, I'm Lucas. I have a small business, and I read a lot about money. Every month, I save ten percent of my profit. How much money do I invest? Not much, but every month. How many stocks do I have? Only five, from big companies. My plan is simple: I don't spend more than my budget, and I invest for the long term.

extra_audio.text: Klaus Weber has a repair shop in Munich. Every month, he makes a budget. He counts how many customers there are. Then he checks how much profit there is. He saves a part of the profit, and he invests a part in stocks. At the end of the year, there is more money for the shop.

vocab.title: Match each word to its meaning
defs: the money you make after you pay all the costs
a small part of a company that you can buy
to keep money and not spend it
a plan for how much money you can spend
to put money in something to make more money later

paras: Klaus Weber has a repair shop in Munich. He is a good mechanic, and he is also good with money. Every month, he sits down with a coffee and makes a budget for the shop.

First, he counts. How many customers were there this month? About four hundred. How many cars are on the lifts now? Six. Then he checks the money. How much profit is there? This month, the profit is twelve thousand euros. The price of spare parts is high, so the profit is not very big.

Klaus has a simple rule. He saves twenty percent of the profit, and he invests ten percent in stocks. He doesn't spend money on things he doesn't need. In five years, he wants a second shop. How much money does he need? About two hundred thousand euros.
